definitions.explanation: The middle area or section of a physical space, region, object, or structure. Used for geographical locations, buildings, documents, and other things that have a discernible center.

examples.japanese: {島|しま}の{中央部|ちゅうおうぶ}に{山|やま}がある。
examples.english: There is a mountain in the central part of the island.

examples.japanese: {建物|たてもの}の{中央部|ちゅうおうぶ}にエレベーターがある。
examples.english: There is an elevator in the center of the building.

examples.japanese: アフリカ{大陸|たいりく}の{中央部|ちゅうおうぶ}には{広大|こうだい}な{熱帯雨林|ねったいうりん}が{広|ひろ}がっている。
examples.english: A vast tropical rainforest stretches across the central part of the African continent.

notes:
Compound of {中央|ちゅうおう} (center) + {部|ぶ} (part/section). A straightforward spatial term that is common in descriptions of geography, architecture, and layout. Slightly more formal and precise than {真|ま}ん{中|なか} (the very center).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {都市|とし}の{中央部|ちゅうおうぶ}: the central part of a city
- {日本|にほん}の{中央部|ちゅうおうぶ}: central Japan
- {胸|むね}の{中央部|ちゅうおうぶ}: the center of the chest

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {中心部|ちゅうしんぶ}: the core/heart — emphasizes being the most important or active area, not just spatially central
- {真|ま}ん{中|なか}: the very middle — more colloquial and emphatic
- {中央|ちゅうおう}: center — the base word without {部|ぶ}, used more broadly including for abstract concepts like government
